modules.title: Start Here
modules.subtitle: What is AI and how does it help you today?

lessons.title: What is AI?
lessons.contentHtml:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to systems that perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence, such as understanding language, recognizing images, making predictions, or generating content.

Modern AI includes large language models (LLMs) that can assist with writing, brainstorming, coding, and more. You don’t need to be technical to get value from AI.

  • AI is a tool: start small and apply it to everyday tasks
  • Always verify important outputs
  • Protect sensitive information

options.label: Tools that can only follow exact instructions

questions.text: Do you need to be technical to benefit from AI?

options.label: No, you can use AI for everyday tasks

lessons.title: Generative AI 101
lessons.contentHtml:
Generative AI creates new content (text, images, audio) from patterns in data. Popular examples include chat assistants and image generators.

Key ideas:

  • Prompt: your instruction to the AI
  • Context: background details or examples you supply
  • Iteration: refining your prompt to improve results

options.label: Your instruction or question to the AI

lessons.title: Everyday AI Uses
lessons.contentHtml:
Practical uses for daily life:

  • Draft emails and summarize articles
  • Plan trips and compare options
  • Create study guides and explain concepts simply

Tip: ask the AI to explain step-by-step and to cite sources when possible.

questions.text: Which is a safe way to start using AI daily?

options.label: Paste confidential data into any app
Summarize a public article and draft a reply

lessons.title: Safety and Ethics
lessons.contentHtml:
AI can make mistakes (hallucinations) and reflect biases. Always review important outputs.

  • Do not share personal or confidential information
  • Verify facts using trusted sources
  • Use AI responsibly and fairly

modules.title: Prompting Basics
modules.subtitle: Get better results with clear instructions

lessons.title: Effective Prompts
lessons.contentHtml:
Structure helps: specify a role, the task, constraints, and format.

Role: You are a helpful travel planner.
Task: Create a 3-day itinerary for Tokyo focused on food.
Constraints: Budget-friendly, kid-friendly, include transit tips.
Format: Return a table with days and activities.

lessons.title: Structured Prompting
lessons.contentHtml: Break down complex tasks into steps and ask the AI to think step-by-step. Provide examples of good outputs.

questions.text: What helps the AI handle complex tasks?

lessons.title: Common Pitfalls
lessons.contentHtml:
• Avoid overly broad prompts
  • Give context and constraints
  • Verify important outputs

questions.text: How do you reduce AI mistakes?

lessons.title: Chat Assistants
lessons.contentHtml: Use popular chat assistants to draft, summarize, translate, and brainstorm. Start with public information and iterate.

questions.text: A good first step with a chat assistant is…

lessons.title: Create Images and Audio
lessons.contentHtml: Generate images and voice drafts. Clearly describe style, subject, and constraints. Check usage rights for public sharing.

questions.text: What should you check before sharing generated media?

lessons.title: Automations
lessons.contentHtml: No-code tools can connect apps and automate tasks. Example: when an email arrives, summarize it with AI, then add action items to your notes app.

options.label: Connecting apps to remove repetitive work

modules.title: Data and Retrieval (RAG)
modules.subtitle: Use your documents with AI, safely

lessons.title: Data Basics
lessons.contentHtml: Good data improves AI results. Organize documents, remove sensitive content, and label versions.

lessons.title: RAG with No‑Code
lessons.contentHtml: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) lets AI answer using your provided documents. Many tools let you upload files and chat with them.

lessons.title: Evaluate Outputs
lessons.contentHtml: For important work, test prompts with examples and check for accuracy, completeness, and helpfulness. Keep a prompt log.

questions.text: What should you do for critical tasks?

lessons.title: AI in Today’s Roles
lessons.contentHtml: Common roles using AI: operations, marketing, support, HR, analysis, and more. Focus on outcomes, not tools.

questions.text: What should you focus on when adopting AI?

options.label: Using as many tools as possible

lessons.title: Capstone: Your AI Assistant
lessons.contentHtml:
Build a personal AI helper for one workflow (e.g., summarizing meeting notes). Define inputs, prompt, and output format. Iterate and evaluate.

  1. Pick a workflow
  2. Draft a structured prompt
  3. Test with examples
  4. Refine and document

questions.text: What is a good capstone goal?

options.label: Learn every AI model in existence
